cnn.title: Trump approves Elon Musk's plan for data centres in space
cnn.desc:
The Trump Administration has approved Elon Musk's plan to launch one million SpaceX satellites into space for AI data centres which will function using solar power. Also: At least thirty people have been killed in the Egyptian capital, Cairo, after a petrol tanker overturned and caught fire on a major ring road. We have a special report on the German boat dealer suspected of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel. A new survey suggests that young people in Britain are having less sex, drinking less alcohol and living with their parents for longer. The US army blows up five tonnes of toxic explosives at a military base in Iowa. Why tiny licence-free cars like the Citroën Ami are gaining in popularity. And the former Duran Duran guitarist, Andy Taylor, has died after a long fight with prostate cancer.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: US announces new tariffs on China and other countries
cnn.desc:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners, including China, the EU, India, and Japan. China is facing the highest rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%. The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year.Also: A hostage crisis involving dozens of people in Colombia has come to a dramatic end. South Africa's president, Cyril Ramaphosa, has won a court battle that has thwarted attempts to impeach him. Leaked data shows that nearly half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the start of the invasion of Ukraine. And one of Africa's most celebrated film stars, the Nigerian actor Pete Edochie, has died.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Huawei has been found guilty of bank fraud in the US
cnn.desc:
The Chinese telecoms company, which has rejected its convictions in the United States, said the allegations were baseless and has threatened to take legal action. The jury in the landmark trial in New York cleared the firm of a more serious charge of racketeering. Also, a hostage crisis is underway in Colombia where gunmen are holding more than a dozen people captive at a supermarket. Senegal have been reinstated as African football champions almost ten months after they beat Morocco. The victims of a brutal conflict in Cameroon's Anglophone regions speak to the BBC. A leader of India's Cockroach movement is prevented from boarding a flight to the UK to speak about the movement. And a Pakistani air force pilot becomes the first astronaut who isn't from China to take part in a Chinese mission in space.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Is Jensen Huang's reinstatement good news for China?
cnn.desc:
The surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang as head of the US chipmaker, Nvidia, has seen mixed reactions worldwide -- but what do people in China make of it all? Also: Malaysia is criticised by human rights groups after saying it will send more migrants back to Myanmar - around two thirds of migrants living in Malaysia are Muslim Rohingyas. The security services in the UK are warning that British companies that provide military supplies to Ukraine could become a military target for Russia. The Bangladeshi government dismisses a demand from the ousted prime minister, Sheikh Hasina, that she be allowed to return from exile. Gisèle Pelicot, the French woman whose husband arranged for dozens of men to rape her while she was unconscious, says she feels humiliated after nude photos were sent to the media to promote a book. The best-selling writer and environmentalist, Robert Macfarlane, on the human superiority complex - the topic he explores in this year's BBC Reith Lectures. cnn.title: Stock markets jump after Nvidia boss reinstated
cnn.desc:
Global stock markets surge after the US chipmaker Nvidia reinstates its chief executive Jensen Huang.  Shares in the firm close sharply higher in New York following the news. Nvidia has come under heavy pressure from President Trump to allow the return of Mr Huang, who resigned earlier this month after admitting having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Also, The head of Nato says the alliance will defend against threats in space following German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a satellite armed with nuclear weapons.We hear of the dangers women face in South Africa, which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world.  Astronomers believe they may be closer than ever to finding another planet in our solar system.Greece repeats its demand that Britain should return the Parthenon sculptures. cnn.desc:
Shares in the tech giant Nvidia soar as its board votes unanimously to reappoint Huang as CEO and President, less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. cnn.title: COP31 in Turkey ends without a deal
cnn.desc:
The UN climate summit in Turkey collapses after the final draft text makes no direct mention of fossil fuels, which proved unacceptable to the European Union and Pacific island countries. Poorer governments had also objected to the lack of clear financial commitments to help them adapt to climate change.
Also: Russia hits Ukrainian energy facilities, straining power supplies and causing widespread power cuts. There's been a suspected drone attack on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi in Libya. In football, the new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino suffers a brutal debut as Liverpool cruise to a 4–0 win. Britain is starting the world's largest trial of artificial intelligence to help breast cancer screening. Israel’s opposition leader says arson attacks in the West Bank amount to Jewish terrorism. The Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari has died aged 89.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Global Story: AI can imitate a human. But can it think like one?
cnn.desc: For decades, computer scientists have been trying to figure out whether computers can think. But with the advent of highly sophisticated chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT…might we finally have our answer? This week we’re introducing The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today. We constantly hear stories about artificial intelligence, but most of them are about where AI is going; in this five-episode series we’re looking at where it came from. Beginning with computer scientist Alan Turing’s famous Turing test in 1950, the quest to verify the existence of machine intelligence has taken on many forms – from the rudimentary chatbots of the 1960s, to the 1997 defeat of a chess grand master by a computer, to IBM Watson’s stint on Jeopardy in the 2010s. But large language models have rendered old methods of measuring machine intelligence obsolete. So how smart is AI, anyway? And will it ever be smarter than us? Tristan Redman and Asma Khalid are joined by Thomas Germain, BBC technology columnist and host of the BBC podcast The Interface. The Global Story brings clarity to politics, business and foreign policy in a time of connection and disruption. For more episodes, just search 'The Global Story' wherever you get your BBC Podcasts.

cnn.title: Deadlock at UN climate summit in Turkey
cnn.desc:
The COP31 summit has gone into a second day of overtime after talks were suspended for the night. There is no agreement in sight with the European Union and Pacific Island nations threatening to walk away without agreeing to a deal because the draft text makes no mention of reducing global demand for fossil fuels. Also: Croatians take to the streets over the death in hospital of a psychiatric patient who was beaten and smothered. We hear from British endurance athlete Lewis Pugh who swam through the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the environmental cost of the war between the US and Iran. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah visits India to try to secure much needed financial aid following devastating floods in the Himalayan nation. And has a maths problem that has puzzled humans for 167 years finally been solved?The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Happy Pod: The 'amazing’ device that controls Tourette's
cnn.desc: We meet 17-year-old Mylo who's taken part in a trial of the watch-like device that suppresses his Tourette's tics. He can even now go to the cinema without fear of causing a disturbance by constantly moving or clearing his throat. Also: the chef in Japan who's known poverty and illness and now offers free meals to people in the position he was once in; the NASA spacecraft, Voyager One, that's become the first human-made object to reach a point one light day from Earth; the surf school in Senegal that's trying to turn its pupils into world champions; and the children with autism and ADHD who've been helped by alpacas. Image: 17-year-old Mylo wearing the device. Credit: BBC News.Our weekly collection of inspiring, uplifting and happy news from around the world.Presenter:  Holly Gibbs. cnn.title: Man found guilty of starting deadly LA wildfire
cnn.desc:
Jonathan Rinderknecht is found guilty of starting the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles, which displaced thousands of people and became one of the most destructive fires in the city’s history. Also: Donald Trump describes his relationship with the leaders of Russia and China as “fantastic”, after meeting with them in Shenzhen. The US president also threatens a ban on American firms building AI data centres overseas, saying they must stay in the US. Russian drones continue to attack Ukraine, with Poland caught in the crossfire. Students in more than 20 European countries protest over education, climate change and military conscription. Cyber security experts in the UK conduct a highly secretive operation to protect its fridges and freezers. Cincinnati Zoo announces the death of the beloved hippo, Fiona. cnn.title: UK agrees deal on closer cooperation with EU
cnn.desc:
UK and EU agree new deal covering food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions. European Commission President, Ursula von der Leyen, said it marked a "turning point" in relations. Also: BBC speaks to people inside the besieged city of Taiz in Yemen. Why the Malaysian government wants to settle 10,000 Rohingyas in Turkey. A group of eight European and developing countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey says a global call to "accelerate the phase-out of fossil fuels" must be restored to the final agreement. Several people are killed and more than a dozen are injured in Ukraine's capital Kyiv, after Russia fires 100 missiles and 400 drones at the city. A new drug, Daraxonrasib, is described as "the biggest leap forward for pancreatic cancer patients in decades".
